channel.title: Information Hub — Daily Intelligence Library
channel.description: Deep, structured briefings written daily by an autonomous multi-provider AI pipeline.

item.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy
item.description: Former Nvidia chief Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick face Senate subpoenas over Huang’s alleged romantic ties to a suspected Chinese intelligence operative, raising fresh concerns about technology transfer and export controls.

item.title: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky praised a pledge by US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to include EU delegates in upcoming peace talks with Russia, marking a diplomatic shift that could give Brussels a stronger voice and bolster Kyiv’s EU aspirations. The move comes amid deepening European security concerns and a new prisoner exchange, while tensions over Starlink restrictions and US

item.title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?
item.description: Labour leader Andy Burnham faces a delicate test as former minister Alan Milburn’s review proposes cuts to disability benefits for 16‑24‑year‑olds. While the party’s internal discipline appears stronger than last year, the final shape of the package will determine whether a modest revolt or a full‑blown rebellion emerges.

item.title: Burnham's push for closer EU ties causes ripples in his party and others
item.description: Labour leader Andy Burnham's advocacy for closer UK-EU relations is dividing his party and prompting scrutiny from other political parties ahead of a week focused on the UK's relationship with the European Union.

item.title: Toki Matter
item.description: Toki AI is an agentic AI platform designed to advance user matters through autonomous task execution, positioning itself as a next-generation AI agent that can handle complex multi-step objectives across personal and professional domains.

item.title: North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI
item.description: The FBI has identified North Korean hackers operating the FaceStealer scheme, which used fake video calls to steal identities and $400 million from cryptocurrency victims over 18 months. The scheme targets cryptocurrency and web3 professionals, and is linked to North Korea's funding of illicit weapons programs.

item.title: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike
item.description: Clashes erupted in Barcelona during Spain's first general strike in 14 years, as tens of thousands protested housing unaffordability and rising living costs. Masked rioters set fires and looted shops while police fired tear gas, underscoring deep social tension ahead of the November 29 parliamentary election.

item.title: Democrat Scott Colom seals historic win in Mississippi Senate race
item.description: Scott Colom became the first Black U.S. Senator from Mississippi in 140 years after a razor‑thin victory over incumbent Cindy Hyde‑Smith, reshaping Southern politics and tightening the Senate’s partisan balance. The win underscores voter fatigue with Republican incumbency and signals a broader Democratic surge in traditionally red states.

item.title: Russia-Ukraine talks turn to post-war security but end without breakthrough
item.description: Trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi focused on a new European security framework, yet produced no concrete agreement. A large‑scale prisoner exchange was confirmed, and US envoys will meet Putin and Zelensky in Moscow and Dublin next week.

item.title: Some under-25s should get less benefits, Milburn review to say
item.description: Alan Milburn’s government‑commissioned review will recommend cutting benefit levels for under‑25s, moving them off main sickness schemes and onto a basic universal‑credit rate, while urging a multi‑billion‑pound push for employment support and training.

item.title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive
item.description: Former parliamentary researcher Chris Cash, acquitted of spying for China, says he was a convenient scapegoat for UK security services while admitting his naïveté in sharing sensitive messages with a Chinese contact. The case underscores escalating UK‑China intelligence tensions and raises questions about how espionage allegations are handled domestically and diplomatically.

item.title: Nod by n8n: The Open‑Source Personal Agent Redefining Automation
item.description: Nod, n8n's new personal AI agent, combines open‑source workflow automation with a dedicated compute environment, positioning it as a low‑cost, self‑hosted alternative to proprietary agentic AI services. Its LLM‑agnostic design, regulatory‑friendly architecture, and community‑driven roadmap make it a strategic tool for developers, enterprises, and regions with tight data‑sovereignty constraints suc

item.title: Three Iran-backed suspects plotted attacks including RAF Fairford incident, US says
item.description: The US Justice Department charged three Iran‑linked operatives for orchestrating a series of terrorist plots across Europe and the US, most notably a failed attack near RAF Fairford in September 2026. The indictment reveals a sophisticated network using coded communications, fake business fronts, and logistical support from Iran’s IRGC, prompting heightened security alerts and diplomatic tensions

item.title: US Army soldier suspected of spying for Russia arrested in UK
item.description: A 41‑year‑old senior US Army soldier was detained near Gloucester on suspicion of passing protected information to Russian intelligence, highlighting insider threats and the growing nexus between traditional espionage and AI‑driven data exploitation.

item.title: US House blocks bid to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, for now
item.description: The House of Representatives defeated a Republican‑led impeachment effort against Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, citing alleged unauthorized war‑making and extrajudicial killings. Democrats can revive the move next year, while President Trump praised Hegseth as a patriot and warned that the vote was a political stunt.

item.title: Tories pledge to cut benefits for children with 'milder cases' of ADHD
item.description: The Conservatives announced plans to save £2.8bn by ending Disability Living Allowance for children with milder behavioural disorders, learning difficulties or ADHD, shifting support to mental‑health services. Labour and advocacy groups condemned the move as a charter for poverty, warning it could increase homelessness and long‑term state costs.

item.title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP
item.description: Liberal Democrat MP Josh Babarinde has introduced a private member's bill, the "St George's Bill", to add black English and Asian English ethnicity options to the UK census, a move backed by Labour’s David Lammy and Conservative Sir James Cleverly. The proposal challenges the current census framework, which only lists English under the white category, and highlights a growing debate over how ethni

item.title: SideKick By Open
item.description: SideKick By Open is a new AI assistant that brings Claude‑like conversational intelligence directly into product workflows, offering real‑time support, code generation, and data analysis for developers and businesses seeking agentic AI capabilities without the overhead of custom models.

item.title: Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy
item.description: President Donald Trump claimed the FBI is probing an alleged affair between Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a woman identified as a Chinese intelligence asset. The episode has rattled Nvidia's market value, raised U.S. security concerns over AI chip exports, and sparked a political flashpoint between Washington and Beijing.

item.title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week
item.description: The UK government is expected to water down its electric vehicle (EV) targets, moving from 80% zero-emission car sales by 2030 to a lower threshold, a move welcomed by carmakers but opposed by environmental groups ahead of COP31.

item.title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
item.description: Nvidia's share price dropped approximately 4% following CEO Jensen Huang's admission of an extramarital affair, amid US intelligence reports suggesting he was targeted by a Chinese espionage campaign. The company announced an independent investigation into the allegations, raising national security concerns and prompting congressional scrutiny while other tech leaders defended Huang's leadership.

item.title: Ukraine peace talks resume with 'some flexibility' by warring sides, US officials say
item.description: Trilateral peace talks between Ukraine, Russia, and the US are resuming in Abu Dhabi with limited flexibility on the Donetsk region, as US officials note that substantive progress requires a new postwar security architecture.

item.title: Surgeon having lunch near Krakow shooting undoubtedly saved officer's life, colleague says
item.description: A surgeon and his colleague, eating near Krakow's Main Market Square, rushed to treat victims when a gunman opened fire, stopping a police officer's fatal bleeding and likely saving his life. The incident, which left six dead and 15 injured, has been classified as a terror attack and sparked broader debates on emergency medical response and far‑right extremism.

item.title: Seven dead and over 100 injured after train collision near Giza, Egypt
item.description: Two passenger trains travelling south from Giza and Cairo collided on the line between Kafr Ammar and Al‑Raqqa, killing at least seven people and injuring more than a hundred. President Abdel Fattah al‑Sisi ordered a probe and promised accountability, while hospitals and the Red Crescent rushed to treat victims.

item.title: Smoky Bacon Crisps and the EU Food Standards Deal: A New Front in UK‑EU Regulatory Tensions
item.description: A pending UK‑EU food‑standards deal could force British snack makers to rename iconic flavours such as smoky bacon crisps, reviving post‑Brexit sovereignty debates. The issue highlights the clash between trade‑saving alignment and domestic regulatory autonomy.

item.title: Nandy rejects claims of politicising Remembrance Sunday after Erasmus row
item.description: Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy defended linking the UK’s return to the EU’s Erasmus+ programme with Remembrance Sunday, insisting the scheme honours wartime sacrifice, while critics from the Conservatives and Reform UK accused her of exploiting the solemn day for EU membership campaigning.

item.title: Agent Clan
item.description: Agent Clan introduces a gesture‑controlled interface for managing Claude Code and Codex AI agents, aiming to streamline developer workflows through natural hand movements. The platform leverages computer‑vision and AI tool integration to enable simultaneous command of multiple agents, positioning itself at the nexus of agentic AI and human‑centric design. Early feedback highlights productivity gai

item.title: Aramco Tower hit in heart of Saudi capital as Houthis launch fresh strikes
item.description: The Houthi movement claimed responsibility for a missile/drone strike that damaged Aramco Tower in Riyadh, marking an escalation in their campaign against Saudi Arabia. While Saudi authorities reported only minor damage, BBC Verify footage suggests more extensive harm, raising concerns about the group's evolving capabilities and the broader regional tensions.

item.title: 'Flat', 'tired', 'cynical': Unusually gloomy Kiwis deliver New Zealand's tightest election in years
item.description: New Zealand voters expressed widespread disillusionment, casting record votes against the two major parties amid economic hardship, housing unaffordability, and declining public services. The election produced a fragmented parliament, with the centrist Opportunity Party emerging as a potential kingmaker and other parties gaining ground, signaling a profound shift in the nation's political landscap

item.title: What we know so far after Krakow gun attack
item.description: A 25‑year‑old Polish man opened fire in Krakow’s Main Market Square, killing six people and wounding sixteen. The attacker, suspected of far‑right ties, was shot by armed officers and later arrested, prompting a nationwide mourning period and renewed debate over extremist radicalisation.

item.title: No clear winner after tight New Zealand general election
item.description: Preliminary results from New Zealand's 2026 general election show a hung parliament with the centre‑right National Party winning 42 seats, 19 short of a majority. Labour secured 36 seats, and smaller parties – Greens, ACT, New Zealand First, the new Opportunity Party and Te Pāti Māori – hold the balance of power, setting the stage for weeks of coalition negotiations.

item.title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker
item.description: Sir Lindsay Hoyle has voiced frustration over the stalled £40 bn Palace of Westminster restoration, warning the project could span six decades and leave the historic building exposed to fire. The public accounts committee labels the situation a “crunch time”, highlighting £420 m of taxpayer loss per year of delay and incomplete safety upgrades. Political and legislative hurdles are now the primary

item.title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham urges businesses to voluntarily disclose pay details in job ads, ahead of upcoming legislation aimed at increasing transparency, preventing discrimination, and narrowing the gender pay gap.

item.title: UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC
item.description: Former EU Brexit negotiator Michel Barnier warns the UK cannot selectively adopt parts of the EU single market, insisting on the four freedoms, as Labour leader Andy Burnham explores closer economic ties with Europe.

item.title: AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values
item.description: AI and tech shares rebounded modestly after a sharp sell‑off triggered by uncertainty over post‑midterm election policy direction, while robust U.S. jobs data offered a partial cushion to investors.

item.title: Two dead after bus crashes in France, officials say
item.description: A bus en route between Lyon and Bourg-en-Bresse crashed in the town of Lent, killing a young girl and an 18‑year‑old man and injuring 43 passengers, including 15 children. French President Emmanuel Macron offered condolences, while authorities launched a homicide investigation and praised the rescue effort.

item.title: Alysis Code
item.description: Alysis Code launches as an open‑source AI coding agent, offering developers a free, community‑driven alternative to proprietary tools like GitHub Copilot. It aims to democratize AI‑assisted development while navigating a tightening regulatory environment for AI.

item.title: Rankfender v3.0
item.description: Rankfender v3.0 introduces an SEO/GEO operating system that unifies human and AI agent workflows, promising smarter keyword targeting and real‑time ranking adjustments across global markets.

item.title: Four midterms takeaways for 2028 White House race
item.description: The 2026 midterms have reshaped the early 2028 presidential calculus, giving Democrats momentum while exposing Republican fissures and highlighting the growing clout of Hispanic voters. Potential candidates from both parties are already positioning themselves amid a backdrop of AI‑driven political analytics and looming regulatory debates.

item.title: New wave of bomb threats hit European airlines
item.description: A coordinated series of hoax bomb threats targeted airlines and media outlets across Europe on Friday, prompting fighter‑jet escorts, evacuations, and heightened security concerns ahead of upcoming EU meetings in Dublin. While no explosives were found, Irish authorities and the EU warn the incidents may be part of a broader disruption campaign, though the responsible parties remain unknown.

item.title: Major tech stocks plunge as US midterms add to fears of AI slowdown
item.description: US midterm elections triggered a market rout that erased roughly $2.5 trillion in tech valuation, as Democrats won control of Congress and signaled tighter regulation of AI data centres. The sell‑off has revived concerns about an AI investment bubble and may reshape global AI policy, including the trajectory of agentic AI and large language models.

item.title: California governor commutes sentences for state's 548 death row inmates
item.description: Governor Gavin Newsom commuted all 548 death sentences to life without parole, citing moral, fiscal, and systemic failures of capital punishment. The move is both a symbolic rebuke of the death penalty and a pragmatic cost‑saving measure, while raising questions about the future of criminal‑justice policy and its intersection with emerging AI governance tools.

item.title: Interest rates hiked to 4% in first increase in over three years
item.description: The Bank of England raised its benchmark rate to 4%, the first rise in more than three years, citing higher energy costs and the ongoing US‑Iran conflict. Policymakers warned the hike may not be the last, while households face higher mortgage repayments and savers see modest gains.

item.title: 'This is a disaster': Angry Republicans blame Trump for midterms defeat
item.description: Republicans are turning on former President Donald Trump after the 2026 midterms, accusing him of costing the party control of Congress through his legacy‑driven agenda and indifference to voter concerns.

item.title: US midterm results a 'victory' for Canadians hopeful of tariff relief
item.description: Canadian leaders see the Democratic midterm sweep as a political opening for tariff relief, though immediate changes are unlikely. The new congressional balance may improve Ottawa’s leverage as on‑again‑off‑again trade talks resume, but many tariffs remain under executive authority.

item.title: Ukraine says bodycam video shows deadly Russian double-tap bombing
item.description: Ukrainian police released a body‑cam video showing two successive Russian glide‑bomb strikes on a shelter in Kamyshuvakha, killing at least 40 civilians. President Zelensky highlighted the attack as another war crime and noted the world's muted response, while diplomatic talks continue in Abu Dhabi and Brussels.

item.title: UK commits to 'time‑bound' talks on slavery apology
item.description: The United Kingdom has agreed to structured, time‑bound talks on the historical harms of the transatlantic slave trade, offering a potential formal apology while ruling out reparations. Diplomats say the dialogue, likely to conclude within a year, aims to address long‑standing demands for recognition and healing.

item.title: Time to focus on cost of living, says PM after US election results
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham urged a global shift toward addressing the cost of living crisis, citing the unresolved US‑Iran conflict as a key driver of rising fuel prices and economic pressure.

item.title: Render Sandboxes – A Cloud‑Native Playground for Agentic AI
item.description: Render Sandboxes offers developers a managed, container‑based environment that can host autonomous AI agents at scale. By coupling low‑latency networking with open‑source tooling, it lowers the barrier for LLM‑driven applications while surfacing new regulatory and security challenges.

item.title: Zero Wire: Cloudflare’s Agentic AI for CVE Exposure Scanning
item.description: Zero Wire, a new Cloudflare product, leverages agentic AI to scan for critical CVEs in real time. By prompting a single agent, security teams can instantly assess exposure across their stack. The solution blends LLM-driven inference with automated remediation workflows, positioning it at the intersection of AI and cybersecurity.
